govdocs-archive_org-nsia-AgendasMemosWar: This FBI memorandum to Warren Commission counsel J. Lee Rankin is a Bureau note to the JFK probe. The declassified memo is a primary source on the investigation. Such memos shaped the commission’s work. The file belongs to the assassination archive.
daniel-deronda: George Eliot's last great novel follows Daniel Deronda — gentleman, musician, and seeker — toward his Jewish destiny, while Gwendolen Harleth dazzles, marries, and suffers. The author's profoundest and most ambitious work. A masterpiece of Victorian fiction, rich and wise. Mirah's singing and Mordecai's visions lift the tale to prophecy.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-achrida: This 1913 reference piece on Achrida — Ohrid, the Balkan see of lake and mountain. Thomas Shahan traces its long primacy. Bulgarian tsars crowned its archbishops. The Balkans' holy city. Its fortress lake mirrors a hundred churches. Samuel's capital kept the old rite.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adam-of-fulda: A 1913 entry on Adam of Fulda — the monk who wrote on music's theory. James Völker notes his treatise. The abbey's choir learned from his rules. A small name in music's long story. His notes guided medieval singers. His Musica survives in a single manuscript.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alabanda: This 1913 reference article on Alabanda — the Carian city, now a titular see. Its bishops' names survive in old lists. Asia Minor's Christian past lives on. A name kept in the hierarchy. The Church forgets no ancient see. Its ruins show the old city's pride.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alonso-andrad: A 1913 entry on Alonso Andrada — the Spanish Jesuit writer. Nazario Perez notes his devotional works. His pen served the missions' cause. The entry preserves his modest fame. A laborer with the pen. His books edified the Spanish missions. His life was prayer as well as prose.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alonso-de-oje: This 1913 reference piece on Alonso de Ojeda — the daring conquistador. Jeremiah Ford tells his voyages. He sailed with Columbus and Vespucci. His sword won lands for Spain. The New World's boldest captain. His colony at Darien began the mainland empire.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amida: This 1913 reference article on Amida — Diyarbekir, the walled city of Mesopotamia. Sophrone Pétridès tells its Christian story. Its black basalt walls still stand. Martyrs and bishops fill its past. The Tigris guards its ancient stones. Its siege starved the Roman garrison.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amphilochius-: A 1913 entry on Amphilochius of Sida — the bishop of Ephesus's council. Thomas Shahan notes his stormy part. He wavered in the Nestorian quarrel. The entry sorts his shifting course. A prelate of troubled times. His see guarded the Pamphylian coast.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-de-an: This 1913 reference piece on Antonio de Andrada — the Jesuit who reached Tibet. Joseph Woods honors his daring journey. He crossed the Himalayas in 1624. The lamas heard his preaching. The first European in the high valleys. His chapel rose in the Tibetan snows.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-attuda: A 1913 entry on Attuda — the Phrygian city, now a titular see. Its bishops grace the old lists. The Maeander guards its ruined site. The Church keeps its ancient name. A see of the highlands. Its coins bore the city's name.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-benda: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Benda — a see of the Albanian mountains. Louis Petit notes its modest record. Its bishops grace the old lists. The Church keeps its ancient name. A see of the Balkan highlands. Its mountains guard the ancient villages.
